title: Genesis Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 16.

questions.question: Who was Sarai's handmaid mentioned in Genesis 16?
questions.correctAnswer: Hagar
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:1 states that Sarai had a handmaid named Hagar, who was an Egyptian.

questions.question: What reason did Sarai give Abram for wanting him to go in unto her maid?
options: The LORD had restrained her from bearing children
She wanted Abram to marry Hagar
She was going to leave Abram
She wanted to travel to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD had restrained her from bearing children
questions.explanation: In Genesis 16:2, Sarai said the LORD had restrained her from bearing children and asked Abram to go in unto her maid.

questions.question: How long had Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan before Sarai gave Hagar to him?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten years
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:3 states that after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan, Sarai gave Hagar to him.

questions.question: What happened after Abram went in unto Hagar?
questions.correctAnswer: She conceived
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:4 tells us Abram went in unto Hagar and she conceived.

questions.question: How did Hagar's attitude toward Sarai change after she conceived?
questions.correctAnswer: She despised her mistress
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:4 explains that when Hagar saw she had conceived, she despised her mistress Sarai.

questions.question: What did Sarai say to Abram about her wrong?
options: Let us pray for a child
questions.correctAnswer: My wrong be upon thee
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:5 records Sarai saying to Abram, "My wrong be upon thee" after Hagar despised her.

questions.question: According to Genesis 16, who did Abram say had the power to deal with Hagar as she pleased?
questions.correctAnswer: Sarai
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:6 shows Abram telling Sarai that her maid is in her hand and she may do to her as it pleaseth her.

questions.question: What did Hagar do when Sarai dealt harshly with her?
questions.correctAnswer: She fled from her face
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:6 states that when Sarai dealt hardly with Hagar, she fled from her face.

questions.question: In Genesis 16, where did the angel of the LORD find Hagar after she fled?
options: By a fountain of water in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: By a fountain of water in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:7 tells that the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a fountain of water in the wilderness.

questions.question: True or False: Sarai was pleased when Hagar conceived a child.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to Genesis 16:4-5, Sarai felt despised by Hagar after she conceived and expressed her displeasure to Abram.

questions.question: True or False: Abram agreed that Sarai could do as she pleased with Hagar.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:6 records Abram telling Sarai that her maid is in her hand and she may do to her as it pleaseth her.

questions.question: True or False: Sarai gave Hagar to Abram immediately after they arrived in Canaan.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:3 specifies Sarai gave Hagar to Abram after he had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan.

questions.question: True or False: Hagar was an Egyptian.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:1 identifies Hagar as an Egyptian handmaid of Sarai.

questions.question: In what order did these events occur in Genesis 16? 1) Sarai gives Hagar to Abram, 2) Hagar conceives, 3) Abram dwells ten years in Canaan, 4) Hagar flees from Sarai.
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:3 states Abram dwelt ten years in Canaan before Sarai gave Hagar to him; then Genesis 16:4 says Hagar conceived; finally Genesis 16:6 says she fled from Sarai.

questions.question: What did Sarai hope to obtain by Abram going in unto Hagar?
questions.correctAnswer: Children by her maid
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:2 records Sarai saying she might obtain children by her maid if Abram went in unto Hagar.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Where did the angel of the LORD find Hagar when she fled from Sarai?
options: By a fountain of water in the wilderness, on the way to Shur
questions.correctAnswer: By a fountain of water in the wilderness, on the way to Shur
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:7 states that the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur.

questions.question: What question did the angel of the LORD ask Hagar when he found her?
options: Whence camest thou? and whither wilt thou go?
Why did you leave your mistress?
questions.correctAnswer: Whence camest thou? and whither wilt thou go?
questions.explanation: In Genesis 16:8, the angel of the LORD asks Hagar, 'Whence camest thou? and whither wilt thou go?' This question prompts Hagar to explain that she is fleeing from Sarai.

questions.question: What instruction did the angel of the LORD give to Hagar regarding her situation with Sarai?
options: Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands
Go to a distant land and start anew
Stay where you are and wait for further instructions
Tell Abram to send Sarai away
questions.correctAnswer: Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:9 records the angel's command to Hagar to return to Sarai and submit to her, teaching the importance of obedience and humility even in difficult circumstances.

questions.question: What promise did the angel of the LORD make to Hagar about her descendants?
options: I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude
Your descendants will be few but blessed
Your seed will be as many as the stars
Your son will be the father of a great nation
questions.correctAnswer: I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude
questions.explanation: The angel's promise in Genesis 16:10 assures Hagar that her offspring will be greatly multiplied, emphasizing God's faithfulness and provision despite present hardships.

questions.question: What name was Hagar instructed to give her son, and why?
options: Ishmael, because the LORD hath heard thy affliction
Esau, because he will be a hunter
Jacob, because he will supplant his brother
questions.correctAnswer: Ishmael, because the LORD hath heard thy affliction
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:11 explains that the angel told Hagar to name her son Ishmael, signifying that God has heard her suffering and affliction.

questions.question: According to Genesis 16:12, how is Ishmael described in relation to others?
options: He will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man's hand against him
He will be a peaceful man, loved by all
He will be a king who unites his brethren
He will be a servant to his brothers
questions.correctAnswer: He will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man's hand against him
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes Ishmael as a wild man, indicating conflict and independence, and that he will dwell in the presence of all his brethren, highlighting the complexity of his future relationships.

questions.question: How does the interaction between verses 9 and 10 teach about obedience and faith in God’s promises?
options: Returning to Sarai (obedience) leads to the promise of multiplied descendants (faith in God’s promise)
Fleeing is the key to receiving God’s promises
questions.correctAnswer: Returning to Sarai (obedience) leads to the promise of multiplied descendants (faith in God’s promise)
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:9 commands Hagar to return and submit, teaching obedience, while 16:10 promises multiplication of her seed, illustrating the connection between obedience and trust in God's promises.

questions.question: What does Genesis 16 teach about trusting God's timing and plans in difficult situations?
options: Even when circumstances seem hard, God’s plans for blessing and multiplication will be fulfilled
Running away from problems is the best solution
questions.correctAnswer: Even when circumstances seem hard, God’s plans for blessing and multiplication will be fulfilled
questions.explanation: Hagar’s fleeing (v8) and the angel’s promise (v10) show that despite hardship and disobedience, God’s plan for blessing Ishmael will stand, teaching trust in God’s sovereign timing.

questions.question: How does Hagar’s naming of God as 'Thou God seest me' (Genesis 16:13) teach about God’s awareness of our struggles?
options: God is always aware and attentive to the afflictions of His people
God only sees when we are obedient
Human suffering is unseen by God
questions.correctAnswer: God is always aware and attentive to the afflictions of His people
questions.explanation: In Genesis 16:13, Hagar acknowledges God’s attentive care despite her distress, teaching believers that God sees and knows their struggles.

questions.question: True or False: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:16 clearly states Abram was fourscore and six (86) years old when Hagar bore Ishmael.

questions.question: True or False: Sarai was pleased when Hagar conceived and treated her kindly.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:4-6 shows that Sarai despised Hagar after she conceived and dealt harshly with her, causing Hagar to flee.

questions.question: True or False: The well where the angel spoke to Hagar was named Beerlahairoi, meaning 'The well of the Living One who sees me.'
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:14 names the well Beerlahairoi, reflecting Hagar’s recognition of God’s watchful care as 'The God who sees me.'

questions.question: What practical lesson about humility can believers learn from Hagar’s story in Genesis 16?
options: Submitting under authority, even when wronged, leads to God’s blessings
Rebellion against authority is always justified
questions.correctAnswer: Submitting under authority, even when wronged, leads to God’s blessings
questions.explanation: The angel’s instruction to Hagar in Genesis 16:9 to return and submit teaches humility and trust in God’s plan despite personal hardship.

questions.question: How does Genesis 16 illustrate God’s care for those who feel abandoned or oppressed?
options: God sends an angel to encourage and promise blessings to Hagar in her distress
God ignores those who run away from their problems
God only helps those who are perfect
God punishes those who feel oppressed
questions.correctAnswer: God sends an angel to encourage and promise blessings to Hagar in her distress
questions.explanation: In verses 7-11, God’s angel finds Hagar in the wilderness, speaks words of encouragement, and promises her numerous descendants, showing God’s compassionate care.

questions.question: Based on Genesis 16, what should a believer do when facing personal conflict and discouragement?
options: Trust God’s promises and submit humbly rather than fleeing
Retaliate against those who wrong them
Ignore the problem and hope it resolves itself
questions.correctAnswer: Trust God’s promises and submit humbly rather than fleeing
questions.explanation: Hagar’s fleeing (v8) contrasts with the angel’s counsel to return and submit (v9), teaching believers to respond to conflict with faith and humility.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 16.

questions.question: What name did Hagar give to the LORD who spoke to her, meaning 'God seeth me'?
questions.correctAnswer: El Roi
questions.explanation: Hagar called the LORD 'El Roi', meaning 'God seeth me', as stated in Genesis 16:13.

questions.question: The well called Beerlahairoi, mentioned in Genesis 16:14, is located between which two places?
questions.correctAnswer: Kadesh and Bered
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:14 states that the well Beerlahairoi was located between Kadesh and Bered.

questions.question: What was the name of the son born to Abram and Hagar?
questions.correctAnswer: Ishmael
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:15 reports that Hagar bore Abram a son, whom Abram named Ishmael.

questions.question: How old was Abram when Ishmael was born?
questions.correctAnswer: Eighty-six years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:16 records that Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the character of Ishmael as prophesied by the angel of the LORD?
options: A peaceful shepherd who dwells in solitude
A wild man whose hand is against every man, and every man's hand against him
A mighty king who rules over many nations
A silent prophet who speaks only to God
questions.correctAnswer: A wild man whose hand is against every man, and every man's hand against him
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:12 describes Ishmael as a wild man with his hand against every man and everyone's hand against him.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Genesis 16:13 where Hagar names God 'El Roi'?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The naming of God as 'El Roi' in Genesis 16:13 forms an inclusio, framing Hagar's encounter by emphasizing God's perception and care, a device that brackets the narrative to highlight God's presence.

questions.question: The name 'Ishmael' means 'God hears.' Which other Bible passage also emphasizes God hearing or answering the afflicted?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 34:17
questions.explanation: Psalm 34:17 speaks of the LORD hearing the cries of the righteous, paralleling the meaning of 'Ishmael' as 'God hears' in Genesis 16:11.

questions.question: In Genesis 16:10, the angel of the LORD promises to multiply Hagar's seed exceedingly. Which New Testament passage reflects God's promise to Abraham about his offspring's multitude?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Romans 4:17, Hebrews 11:12, and Galatians 3:16 all affirm God's promise to Abraham about his numerous offspring, echoing the promise made to Hagar in Genesis 16:10.

questions.question: The term 'Beerlahairoi' in Genesis 16:14 is a Hebrew compound word. What does it literally mean?
options: Well of the God who sees me
questions.correctAnswer: Well of the God who sees me
questions.explanation: The Hebrew compound 'Beerlahairoi' literally means 'Well of the God who sees me,' reflecting Hagar's experience described in Genesis 16:14.

questions.question: Which cultural practice from the ancient Near East is illustrated by Sarai giving her maid Hagar to Abram to bear children on her behalf?
options: Polygamy as a sign of wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Surrogate motherhood to produce offspring
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:2-3 shows Sarai offering Hagar as a surrogate to bear children, a recognized ancient Near Eastern practice when a wife was barren.

questions.question: What is the significance of Hagar fleeing from Sarai after conceiving, in terms of the chapter's theme of divine providence?
options: It shows human failure without God's intervention
It emphasizes God's care for the marginalized
It highlights the dangers of disobedience
It foreshadows future conflict between descendants
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes God's care for the marginalized
questions.explanation: Hagar fleeing and being found by the angel of the LORD in Genesis 16:7-9 highlights divine providence and care for the marginalized, a key theme in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: Abram opposed Sarai’s plan to have a child through Hagar and refused to comply with her request.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:2 states Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai, indicating he complied with her plan.

questions.question: True or False: Hagar's naming of God as 'El Roi' reveals an important theological theme of God's omnipresence and care.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:13 shows Hagar recognizing God as 'El Roi', meaning 'God sees me,' underscoring God's omnipresence and personal care.

questions.question: Which New Testament figure is connected typologically with Ishmael as a son born according to the flesh, contrasted with a son born according to promise?
questions.correctAnswer: Paul
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:21-31 uses Ishmael and Isaac typologically to contrast children of the flesh and children of promise, a teaching attributed to Paul.

questions.question: Which literary structure helps to highlight the contrast between Sarai’s and Hagar’s experiences in Genesis 16?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Genesis 16 exhibits a chiasm structure contrasting Sarai’s barrenness and Hagar’s pregnancy, focusing the narrative on God's unfolding plan.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological truth does Sarai's barrenness and her giving Hagar to Abram illustrate about human limitations and God's providence?
options: Human inability to control God's timing for blessing
The absolute certainty of human fertility
God's immediate fulfillment of all human desires
The irrelevance of faith in God's promises
questions.correctAnswer: Human inability to control God's timing for blessing
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:1-3 shows Sarai's barrenness and her decision to give Hagar to Abram, indicating human limitation in fulfilling God's promise by natural means. This highlights reliance on God's providence rather than human effort.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning sin and its consequences is revealed when Hagar flees from Sarai after being mistreated?
options: Sin leads to broken relationships and flight from authority
Sin has no real effect on interpersonal dynamics
Sin always results in immediate physical death
Sin is only a personal matter without social consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to broken relationships and flight from authority
questions.explanation: In Genesis 16:6, Sarai deals harshly with Hagar, causing her to flee. This illustrates how sin disrupts relationships and leads to estrangement, a biblical principle about the social impact of sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by the angel of the LORD's reassurance to Hagar that her seed will be multiplied exceedingly?
options: God's mercy and faithfulness to His promises
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and faithfulness to His promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:10 records the angel of the LORD promising to multiply Hagar's seed, showing God's merciful faithfulness to fulfill His covenantal promises despite human failure.

questions.question: How does the naming of Ishmael by the angel connect to God's attribute of omniscience and care?
options: It shows that God hears and knows the affliction of the afflicted
It indicates God's forgetfulness of human names
It reveals God's indifference to individual suffering
It demonstrates God's anger without compassion
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that God hears and knows the affliction of the afflicted
questions.explanation: In Genesis 16:11, the angel names the child Ishmael, meaning 'God hears,' indicating God's omniscience and compassionate care for those who suffer, consistent with Psalm 34:18.

questions.question: What does the description of Ishmael as a 'wild man' with his hand against every man illustrate about human nature and conflict?
options: The reality of enmity and struggle among humanity due to sin
The perfect harmony among all peoples
The absence of conflict in God's plan
The inevitability of peace without struggle
questions.correctAnswer: The reality of enmity and struggle among humanity due to sin
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:12 describes Ishmael's nature, reflecting the doctrine that sin results in ongoing conflict and hostility in human relationships, a fallen condition seen throughout Scripture.

questions.question: How does Hagar's statement 'Thou God seest me' reveal a key aspect of God's character?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipresence and personal attentiveness
questions.explanation: In Genesis 16:13, Hagar acknowledges God as 'El Roi,' meaning God sees her, demonstrating God's omnipresence and intimate knowledge of individual human plight, a foundational attribute.

questions.question: What does the location of Beerlahairoi signify in the narrative and theological structure of Genesis 16?
options: A divine provision and encounter point in the wilderness
A place of judgment and condemnation
questions.correctAnswer: A divine provision and encounter point in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:14 names the well Beerlahairoi, meaning 'well of the Living One who sees me,' symbolizing God's provision and presence in place of human distress, consistent with wilderness theophanies.

questions.question: In what way does Abram’s age at Ishmael’s birth (eighty-six years) contribute to understanding God's timing in salvation history?
options: It emphasizes that God's promises are fulfilled according to His sovereign timing
It suggests human effort is sufficient to realize promises
It shows that God's promises are immediate and without delay
It indicates that age is irrelevant in biblical narratives
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes that God's promises are fulfilled according to His sovereign timing
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:16 notes Abram's age, underscoring that God's covenantal promises unfold in His perfect timing, highlighting divine sovereignty over human chronology.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about human responsibility and divine command is conveyed by verses 8-9, where the angel instructs Hagar to return and submit to Sarai?
options: God calls for obedience and submission even amid hardship
questions.correctAnswer: God calls for obedience and submission even amid hardship
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:8-9 show the angel commanding Hagar to return and submit, teaching the doctrine that divine will often includes calls to faithful obedience within difficult social structures.

questions.question: What theological significance arises from the synthesis of Sarai’s initiative in verses 2-3 and God’s promise to multiply Ishmael’s seed in verses 10-12?
options: Human attempts to fulfill God's promises do not thwart His sovereign plans
Human plans always override divine promises
God abandons those who act independently
God's promises depend entirely on human action
questions.correctAnswer: Human attempts to fulfill God's promises do not thwart His sovereign plans
questions.explanation: Verses 2-3 show Sarai’s human initiative, while 10-12 reveal God’s sovereign multiplication of Ishmael’s seed, teaching that human imperfection cannot frustrate God's ultimate purposes.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's involvement with Hagar shows favoritism and injustice. What does Genesis 16:7-13 actually teach about God's character in this context?
options: God is compassionate and attentive to the marginalized and oppressed
God is indifferent to human suffering
God supports only the socially powerful
questions.correctAnswer: God is compassionate and attentive to the marginalized and oppressed
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:7-13 shows God’s angel finding Hagar, comforting her, and promising blessing, illustrating God's justice and care for the lowly, refuting claims of divine favoritism.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Abram and Sarai in verses 5-6 reveal about human tendencies in dealing with conflict and accountability?
options: Humans often shift blame rather than assume responsibility
Humans always act righteously in conflict
Humans are indifferent to interpersonal tensions
Humans always seek divine judgment first
questions.correctAnswer: Humans often shift blame rather than assume responsibility
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:5-6 records Sarai blaming Abram and Abram deferring to Sarai’s authority, illustrating human tendencies to evade direct accountability in relational conflicts.

questions.question: How does Ishmael's role as one who 'shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren' (v.12) contribute to the biblical theology of God's unfolding covenantal plan?
options: It foreshadows the complex relationships and promises involving Abraham's descendants
It indicates Ishmael replaces Isaac as the covenant heir
It denies God's involvement with Ishmael's lineage
It suggests Ishmael is excluded from any divine blessing
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the complex relationships and promises involving Abraham's descendants
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:12 shows Ishmael dwelling among his brethren, reflecting the unfolding complexity of Abraham's seed and God's covenantal plan involving multiple peoples.

questions.question: What is the doctrinal implication of Sarai giving Hagar to Abram 'to be his wife' after ten years in Canaan, regarding faith and human initiative?
options: Human impatience can lead to actions that complicate God's promises
Human initiatives always align perfectly with God's plan
God condemns all human decisions in faith contexts
questions.correctAnswer: Human impatience can lead to actions that complicate God's promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:3 shows Sarai's decision after waiting ten years, illustrating that human impatience can lead to problematic efforts that intersect with divine promises.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Genesis 16 fit into the broader redemptive story of Scripture concerning God's covenant promises?
options: It demonstrates God's faithfulness to promise despite human failure and sin
It shows that God's promises are conditional on human perfection
It indicates a rejection of all covenant promises
It suggests God's covenant is revoked due to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God's faithfulness to promise despite human failure and sin
questions.explanation: Genesis 16 as a whole shows that despite Sarai and Abram's flawed actions, God remains faithful to His promises, a key theme in biblical redemptive history (cf. Romans 4:20-21).
